t: This is Balls Pond Road Cemetery, a Jewish burial ground on Kingsbury Road, founded in 1843 and owned by West London Synagogue. Early members of that congregation, including the de Stern, Goldsmid and Mocatta families, are buried here. So are the writer Annette Salaman, the philanthropist Rachel, Countess d'Avigdor, and the banker David Quixano Henriques. The ashes of Amy Levy are here too. She was a poet and novelist, one of the first Jewish students at Cambridge, and the first Jewish woman cremated in England. The last burial was in 1951, and the cemetery has been Grade II listed since 2020.
